title: UpDLRM: Accelerating Personalized Recommendation using Real-World PIM Architecture
problem: Embedding layers in DLRMs suffer from intensive memory bandwidth requirements for irregular memory accesses during embedding lookups, creating a performance bottleneck that limits inference latency for recommendation tasks.
motivation: DLRMs are widely deployed for large-scale recommendation systems and accelerating their inference latency is critical for real-world deployment.
method: UpDLRM leverages the UPMEM DPU, a real-world processing-in-memory device, to provide high aggregated memory bandwidth for irregular embedding lookups. The system optimizes embedding table partitioning to achieve balanced workloads and efficient multi-level data caching within the DPU's memory hierarchy, exploiting the parallel nature of DPU memory to handle concurrent irregular accesses.
key_novelty: First practical application of real-world UPMEM DPU processing-in-memory hardware to accelerate DLRM inference by providing high aggregated memory bandwidth for irregular embedding lookups.
contributions: First system design utilizing UPMEM DPU for accelerating DLRM inference deployment on real-world hardware
Embedding table partitioning strategy optimized for DPU architecture to achieve balanced workload distribution and efficient caching
Experimental validation demonstrating significant inference latency reduction compared to CPU-only and CPU-GPU hybrid systems on real-world datasets
